title: Camp 4 close: back to Galilee
hookLine: the young man said: he's going ahead of you to Galilee, back where it all began (Mark 16:7)

lines: HE GOETH BEFORE YOU INTO GALILEE.
cards: Have you ever gone back to your hometown after something big happened? The streets are the same. The diner is the same.

You're not. At the empty tomb, the young man in white gave the women a message for the disciples. In the King James Bible: "he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you."
Not to Rome. Not to the temple. Back to Galilee: the lake, the boats, the nets, the little towns where it all began.

teach.b: For seventy-five days, this camp has read Mark's Gospel in order, a few verses at a time. It began with a single line: the beginning of the good news. Then the heavens torn open, and fishermen told to leave the nets.
Friends dug through a roof. A leper heard I am willing. A sower threw seed everywhere, and Jesus slept on a cushion in a storm.
A little girl heard talitha koum, get up. Five thousand were fed, and a woman told she was a dog answered back, and her daughter was healed.

At Caesarea Philippi came the question at the center of the book: who do you say I am? Then the road to Jerusalem: take up your cross; a blind man named Bartimaeus asked to see; a widow gave all she had.

teach.h: FROM THE NETS TO THE EMPTY TOMB.
teach.b: And in these last days of the camp: perfume poured out, bread broken, abba in the garden, Peter weeping by the fire, a crown of thorns, the women who stayed, and an empty tomb.
Mark's ending sends the disciples back to the beginning.

teach.h: BACK TO GALILEE, BACK TO CHAPTER ONE.
teach.b: Some readers think Mark wants his readers, too, to go back to chapter one and read it again, knowing how it ends.
The disciples misunderstood again and again the first time through. Read again, the same stories look different.
The very first verse, in the King James Bible: "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God." The beginning, as if the whole book is only the start.
Tomorrow a new camp begins, camp five, the depths, opening with Jesus sitting down on a mountain to teach.

how: Churches that follow a lectionary read through one Gospel across a year of Sundays; in the three-year cycle shared by Catholics and a number of Protestant churches, Mark is the Gospel of the second year.

o: Mark's first word, where his ending sends you back
the opening of Genesis, where God makes the world
the first day of the week, when the tomb was found

camp four read Mark in order, a few verses a day
from 1:1 to the end of chapter 16.

games.q: the tomb is empty, and a young man in white says: he goes before you. where does he tell the disciples to go?
games.why: "he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him." back to the lake and the nets, to begin again knowing more.

practice: Open a Bible, if you can, to the first verse of Mark and read it slowly, the way you'd now, after everything, noticing which word lands differently; if you can't, say it quietly to yourself.
Then let the one story from this camp that stays with you most come up on its own. If you pray, you can give thanks for it.
